dualStream.where: YouTube Studio > Stream settings > Dual stream toggle
dualStream.note: Soft issue, not worth chasing. No field for it exists anywhere in youtube/v3 (checked against the discovery document and every part of liveBroadcasts and liveStreams), so it can be neither set nor read here. It is also only toggleable while a stream is in its starting phase, not once running - which on an 8h rotation means a few unattended minutes every cycle. Treat it as off and move on.
dualStream.rechecked: 2026-09-19 (T-34-era session). Re-verified against the CURRENT surface, not the 2.x note: the youtube/v3 discovery document (revision 20260914) has no dual/vertical/aspect field anywhere; the LIVE broadcast's full contentDetails key list is boundStreamId, boundStreamLastUpdateTimeMs, closedCaptionsType, enableAutoStart, enableAutoStop, enableClosedCaptions, enableContentEncryption, enableDvr, enableEmbed, enableLowLatency, latencyPreference, monitorStream, projection, recordFromStart; and liveStreams.cdn.ingestionInfo exposes only streamName, ingestionAddress, backupIngestionAddress, rtmpsIngestionAddress, rtmpsBackupIngestionAddress - there is no vertical key to push to. The Live Streaming API revision history through 2026-08 has no dual-stream addition (it lists categoryId, availabilityConfig, monetizationDetails/midrolls and errors). Google's own route (dual-format support for third-party encoders, announced 2026-08-20) is: pick 'Encoder' instead of 'Auto' in the Dual stream box in the Live Control Room and type a SECOND stream key by hand; the choice is fixed when the stream goes live and cannot be removed afterwards. So it is per-broadcast, Studio-only, and un-undoable - the exact opposite of automatable. It resets every rotation because prepare_broadcast() creates a brand-new broadcast and a new broadcast inherits nothing. Options considered and rejected: driving the Studio UI from the streamer (needs a logged-in Google web session on the machine - a credential exposure this project deliberately avoids - and breaks on any UI change); a second standalone vertical broadcast via the API (a different product: separate URL and chat, no shared notification, plus a second encode on a 2015 dual-core i5 already reporting videoIngestionStarved). ONE EXPERIMENT COULD STILL OVERTURN THIS: toggle Dual stream on by hand for a live broadcast, then list liveStreams again - if YouTube creates a second liveStream resource for the vertical feed, there may be a bindable path after all. Do that before spending more time here.

_note: Reference configuration for every new broadcast. stream.sh captures from the outgoing broadcast at each rotation and enforces this onto the new one. Anything under 'manual' cannot be automated - see each note.
